title: Negative Ext vanishing on a basis and the sheaf of derived Hom
statement: Let $f:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], let $\mathcal B$ be a basis for the topology of $Y$, and let $K,L\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, where $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A basis means a family of open sets such that every open set is a union of members. Restriction to an open is induced by restricting complexes of module sheaves termwise; the module category on that open uses the restricted structure sheaf. Sheaf on $Y$ means sheaf on the site of opens with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. If $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_{f^{-1}(V)})}(K|_{f^{-1}(V)},L|_{f^{-1}(V)}[i])=0$ for every $V\in\mathcal B$ and every integer $i<0$, then the same vanishing holds for every open $V\subseteq Y$, and the assignment $V\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_{f^{-1}(V)})}(K|_{f^{-1}(V)},L|_{f^{-1}(V)})$ is a sheaf of abelian groups on $Y$.

proof.text: Work in a universe containing the opens and module values; the structure sheaves are commutative, as required by the ringed-site tools. Put $A=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(K,L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. By [lem-trf-open-ext-hypercohomology-comparison], for every integer $i$ the presheaf $V\mapsto H^i(f^{-1}V,A)$ is canonically isomorphic to the local shifted-Hom presheaf in the statement, with its canonical restriction maps. Inverse images of open inclusions are open inclusions, so the restriction compatibility applies to all opens of $Y$. For $W\subseteq V$ in $Y$, let $j:f^{-1}W\hookrightarrow f^{-1}V$. Apply the comparison square at $j$. Before the canonical shift identification, its right restriction is $a\mapsto e_K^{-1};S_j(a);e_{L[i]}$ from [def-trf-ringed-derived-open-hom-restriction], applied to $K,L[i]$. Thus it uses exactly the canonical restrictions of the statement, also for nonzero $i$.

Put $B=Rf_*A$. By [lem-trf-unbounded-direct-image-section-presheaf], for every integer $i$ the presheaf $P_i(V)=H^i(f^{-1}V,A)$ is canonically isomorphic to $V\mapsto H^i(V,B)$, and $P_i^\#$ is the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal H^i(B)$. For $i<0$, Step 1 and the hypothesis say $P_i(V)=0$ for all $V\in\mathcal B$. Every map from $P_i$ to an abelian sheaf $F$ is zero: for any open $W$ and $s\in P_i(W)$, its image restricts to zero on the covering of $W$ by basis members contained in $W$, so the sheaf equalizer axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] makes its image zero on $W$. By the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], maps from $P_i^\#$ to $F$ are therefore unique. Set $F=P_i^\#$; its identity equals its zero endomorphism, so $P_i^\#=0$. Hence the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal H^i(B)$ has zero sections on every open. Its module sections are the same groups, so $\mathcal H^i(B)=0$ for all $i<0$.

proof.text: By Step 2, $B=Rf_*A$ has $\mathcal H^i(B)=0$ for $i<0$. Apply [lem-trf-connective-hypercohomology-sheaf] on the ringed space $Y$. It gives $H^i(V,B)=0$ for every open $V$ and $i<0$, and a canonical isomorphism of abelian presheaves $V\mapsto H^0(V,B)$ with the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal H^0(B)$.

For every open $V\subseteq Y$, combine the comparisons of Steps 1 and 2 with Step 3:
$$\operatorname{Hom}(K|_{f^{-1}V},L|_{f^{-1}V}[i])\cong H^i(f^{-1}V,A)\cong H^i(V,B).$$
The right side is zero for $i<0$. In degree $0$ these comparisons commute with restriction, and identify the Hom presheaf in the statement with $V\mapsto\Gamma(V,\mathcal H^0(B))$. It is therefore a sheaf of abelian groups. This also handles $V=\varnothing$: module sheaves have the zero group of sections there by the empty-cover equalizer axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], so the sheaf condition includes the empty cover. No closure of $\mathcal B$ under intersections is needed: all uses of the basis were its coverings of each open by basis members contained in it.
